title: 60 Minutes whistleblower told to 'turn down the temperature'

tellings.quote:
>> But you saw in 60 minutes that guy who
said he quit said uh uh that woman came
to him and said, "We got to turn down
the temperature on this thing."
So one of the very first things that I heard when I arrived at the AHI Unit was, "Our job is to bring down the temperature on AHI at headquarters."
All of this, he says, led him to resign.

plain: The story is that a government insider who quit said he was told from above to calm things down, in Haseltine's words to "turn down the temperature on this thing." A former senior NSA official named Eric Haseltine tells Michels about it, saying he saw it on the CBS programme 60 Minutes, where a man who resigned said a woman came to him with that message. Haseltine does not say which report he means. A likely match is the 60 Minutes report by Scott Pelley aired on March 8, 2026, about a device that may be tied to Havana Syndrome, the unexplained injuries the CIA calls anomalous health incidents. In it a former CIA officer recalls that one of the first things he heard on joining the unit was: "Our job is to bring down the temperature on AHI at headquarters," and the report says that all of this "led him to resign." The broadcast does not say who spoke the line or that it was a woman, and its subject is Havana Syndrome rather than UFOs; the 2021 60 Minutes report on UFOs has no such line. Haseltine raises it as a sign that officials work to play down troubling subjects.

discussion.by: U.S. military tested device that may be tied to Havana Syndrome on rats, sheep, confidential sources say (60 Minutes)
discussion.text: The teller does not say which 60 Minutes report he means; if it is the 60 Minutes report on Havana Syndrome of 8 March 2026, a former CIA officer who resigned says that when he arrived at the CIA's unit for anomalous health incidents (Havana Syndrome) he heard "Our job is to bring down the temperature on AHI at headquarters"; the report does not say who said it or that it was a woman, and its subject is Havana Syndrome, not UFOs. The 60 Minutes UFO report of May 2021 holds no such line.
